fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so arriving units can identify it quickly, especially at night.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation back from the sides of the main residence so responders can move around the building on foot.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around it.
• Keep a clear path along the perimeter fencing to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.
• If the perimeter fence has a gate, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-Box or lockbox so responders can access the rear without cutting the fence.
• Mark any gate locations on the fence line with a reflective indicator so responders can find them quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so arriving units have room to stage equipment.
• Maintain the walkway between the street and the front entry clear of obstacles so responders can move quickly to the front door.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the house.
• Clear dead leaves, needles, and loose plant material from the roof and gutters.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep the full width and height clear for vehicle access.
• Cut back shrubs along the driveway edges that narrow the travel path.
• Remove dead material from scattered shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath trees near the house clear of dead leaves and fallen branches.
